title: The onion trade that looked profitable but wasn't
summary: Lasalgaon → Azadpur, January 2024: a ₹156 per quintal median price gap on 26 matched days. After modeled costs: −₹258 per quintal on the typical day.
why_selected: Chosen automatically for January 2024: one of AGRINET's documented trade corridors with 26 matched report days.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices; sale matched to the first destination report 1–3 days after transit
caveats: Hypothetical: no actual shipment is claimed.
Modal prices may mix varieties and grades (mostly FAQ).
Costs are survey values and assumptions, not quotes.
OSRM car profile; truck route not verified.

scenes.headline: January 2024
scenes.caption: Lasalgaon (Nashik) is India's best-known onion auction; Azadpur (Delhi) is the largest terminal market it feeds, a link the RBI paper describes.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 26 matched days, Lasalgaon reported a median ₹1,625 per quintal; Azadpur reported ₹1,594 2 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹156/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹156 per quintal and was positive on 65% of days.

scenes.headline: 1,115 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 1,115 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~13 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 2 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹240/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹258 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹438 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 1 of 26 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 5 of 26 days, averaging −₹257 per quintal; 5 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: The ₹156 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹240/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: The ₹156 gap looked tempting, but on the typical day modeled costs absorbed it. A gap on a price board is not a margin.

scenes.headline: November 2024
scenes.caption: The short road from Nashik's onion belt to Mumbai's wholesale market at Vashi.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: On 23 matched days, Lasalgaon reported a median ₹4,640 per quintal; Vashi New Mumbai reported ₹4,450 1 days later.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹-650/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gross gap was ₹-650 per quintal and was positive on 13% of days.

scenes.headline: 217 km by road
scenes.caption: Routed road distance 217 km (OpenStreetMap car routing, ~3 driving hours). Trucks are slower; we allow 1 days.

scenes.headline: Now add the costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹47/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. Modeled net on the typical (median) day: −₹1,136 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Stress test
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day becomes −₹1,342 per quintal.

scenes.headline: Hindsight vs. a real trader
scenes.caption: With perfect hindsight, 0 of 23 days cleared modeled costs. A trader using only reports available on the day would have shipped on 1 of 23 days, averaging −₹182 per quintal; 1 of those shipments lost money.

scenes.headline: The lesson
scenes.caption: Here the source market was dearer than the destination on most days. Produce would not have flowed this way on price alone.

assumptions.value: scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹47/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days

conclusion: Here the source market was dearer than the destination on most days. Produce would not have flowed this way on price alone.
